transcript:
MEETING HEADER
Date: 2026-07-24 14:27 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Alex Morgan (CTO - StridePath), Priya Shah (Platform Lead), Ben Torres (Security), Jin Woo (ML Engineer)

AUTOGEN SUMMARY (may be incomplete):
- Quick intro and goals: evaluate Redwood for their inference layer; see fastest path to first token for a PLG flow, and understand criteria for reserved/dedicated or private deployment.
- Security: SOC2, SAML/SSO, KMS/HSM questions.
- Performance: baseline latency targets 80-120ms p50 for short completions; cost sensitivity for high-QPS embedding workloads.

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey thanks everyone for joining, uh I'm Maya from Redwood, I'll run the quick agenda — intros, goals, current stack, then tradeoffs between quickstart hosted versus reserved/dedicated or private VPC, and then next steps.
[00:12] Alex (StridePath): Yeah thanks Maya, I'm Alex, CTO. We're trying to get a PLG experiment live in two weeks if possible, need to know TTFT and what you give us out of the box.
[00:20] Priya: Hi, Priya here - platform. We manage infra ramp and network, so VPC and private connectivity questions up front please.
[00:28] Maya: Totally, good to know. Ravi, quick intro?
[00:30] Ravi (Redwood): Hey all, Ravi - solutions engineer, I'll be the technical owner on any bench that we run. We usually provide a quickstart flow with credits and sample SDKs, and can run a small benchmark.
[00:38] Jin (StridePath): Jin - ML eng. Our main model use is retrieval-augmented generation and embeddings for similarity search, high QPS on embeddings, smaller chat completions.
[00:47] Ben (StridePath): Ben - security. We'll need SOC2, ISO docs, data retention and KMS details. Also concerned about customer PII hitting hosted service.
[00:55] Maya: Great - so first, TTFT. If you sign up self-serve we can get you to first token in under an hour typically: sign up, apply credits, run the SDK sample. For demo/pilot we'll allocate 50k free credits so you can exercise embedding and a small chat flow.
[01:10] Alex: Under an hour sounds optimistic, is that real or like portal time? We need to know if our engineers can integrate in a day.
[01:15] Maya: Real—portal + SDK + sample app. For a proper integration, expect a 1-2 day sprint depending on auth and network. For private/VPC there's more lead time.
[01:26] Priya: How does private work — do we run the inference inside our VPC or you provide a private control plane?
[01:32] Lena (Redwood): We offer Redwood Private: customer-managed VPC peering or private endpoints. You can run inference nodes in your cloud account (we provide AMIs/helm charts for on-prem), or use our private tenancy where control plane is in a customer-dedicated instance.
[01:47] Priya: Okay, and what's the gap between dedicated and private?
[01:50] Ravi: Dedicated is reserved capacity in Redwood's environment—isolated GPU pool under your tenancy but still managed by Redwood. Private is full network isolation and optional on-prem where control plane sits inside your network. Dedicated gives faster time-to-scale, private gives maximum isolation.
[02:04] Alex: Performance-wise do you have numbers? We aim for p50 under 100ms for short completions and embeddings under 30ms ideally for vector generation — is that crazy?
[02:15] Ravi: 30ms for embeddings is aggressive depending on model size and batch. For smaller embedding models we hit low double-digit ms at optimized quantized runtime on A100-like hardware; on shared hosted the p50 can be 30-70ms depending on batch and batching policy. For chat completions 80-120ms p50 for trimmed tokens is realistic on dedicated.
[02:33] Jin: What about KV cache — how do you manage multi-tenant cache with session affinity? Seems like a big factor for latency.
[02:40] Ravi: We have continuous batching and per-tenant KV cache management, but caveat our transcriptions sometimes say K V cash, sorry. The important bit is session affinity for KV cache on dedicated/private is easier — we guarantee sticky routing for a session and can TTL caches to optimize hit rates.
[02:55] Ben: For SOC2, can you share your report? And SSO? We use Okta/SAML and need SCIM provisioning.
[03:02] Maya: Yep, we'll share the SOC2 Type II and our security whitepaper. We support SAML SSO and SCIM, RBAC is configurable. For KMS, we integrate with customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and HSM options for private deployments.
[03:16] Alex: Cost — how do we balance latency vs cost? We have a heavy embedding workload; we care about cost per 1M embeddings.
[03:22] Maya: On Redwood Optimize we'll recommend model quantization and batching profiles. Hosted is typically cheapest to start due to pooling; dedicated reduces tail latency but costs more. For high-volume embeddings, dedicated with optimized quantization often reduces per-unit cost because we can tune kernel and batched throughput.
[03:39] Priya: If we do the quickstart first, are we locked in to hosted? Could we move to dedicated or private later without API changes?
[03:45] Lena: You won't be locked in. The API is consistent across hosted/dedicated/private. You can pin model versions and rollout policies; moving to private mostly involves network/workload migration and capacity plan — the same SDK and endpoints with config changes.
[03:58] Jin: For the pilot bench, can you run a 5k-10k embedding run and share latency distribution and GPU utilization?
[04:05] Ravi: Yes — typical approach: we run a controlled bench using your sample payloads and record token/embedding latency, p50/p95/p99, and cost per embedding. We'll also provide a script so you can reproduce in your account for private.
[04:18] Alex: Great. One question on compliance — data retention and deletion APIs? We need to ensure log retention policy and the ability to purge customer data on demand.
[04:25] Maya: We have retention controls and deletion APIs; for private deployments you can entirely control data residency. For hosted we offer controls, and we can isolate logs per account and provide audit logs. We'll include that in the security pack.
[04:36] Ben: Encryption at rest and in transit? Key rotation?
[04:39] Lena: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest; customer-managed keys via KMS and rotation policies supported. We can provide more detailed config in the security doc.
[04:48] Alex: What's the SLA on dedicated? We need predictable throughput for peak retail hours.
[04:53] Ravi: We offer SLA-backed latency windows and uptime guarantees on Dedicated with reserved capacity contracts. For PLG hosted it's best-effort but we have fallback routing across regions.
[05:03] Priya: If we choose private on AWS, what's the onboarding timeline?
[05:07] Maya: Private onboarding usually takes 3-6 weeks for full private/on-prem installs depending on network approvals, otherwise VPC private endpoints can be done in 1-2 weeks. Dedicated spins up faster — often under a week.
[05:16] Jin: Any pre-built SDKs we should look at? We use Python and Node.
[05:19] Ravi: We have Python/Node/Go SDKs, plus a sample retrieval-augmented generation repo and an embeddings benchmark harness. I'll drop links.
[05:26] Alex: On the free credits — is that transferable to production? Like, do they convert to discounts if we sign a contract?
[05:31] Maya: Credits are for onboarding and POC; they don't auto-convert to production but we can roll them into contract negotiations as one-time credits or pilot allowances.
[05:39] Ben: A practical question — network egress for embeddings if we do private in our VPC, do we still need to send data to Redwood managed infra?
[05:45] Lena: For private with nodes in your cloud, data stays in your account. For dedicated it's in Redwood-managed infra but isolated; for hosted it's in Redwood's multi-tenant environment. We'll detail the exact flow in the security doc.
[05:58] Priya: Ok, pilot scope — two-week bench: 1) baseline embeddings 10k items, 2) chat flow smoke test, 3) network connectivity test for VPC/private, 4) security review. Is that doable?
[06:10] Maya: Yes. Proposed timeline: allocate credits today; run bench next week; deliver results and security pack by end of week two.
[06:19] Alex: Who will be our go-to on Redwood side for the bench?
[06:22] Maya: Ravi will lead the bench, Lena on security/networking. I'll be AE and coordinate.
[06:27] Jin: We may want a comparison to OpenAI embeddings for cost/latency — do you have that kind of benchmark?
[06:33] Ravi: We do comparative benchmarks for common model families; I'll include sample tables but note they vary by model and quantization; we prefer to run your payload for apples-to-apples.
[06:41] Alex: Any blockers on our side? We'll need Prisma egress rules and a quick change to our Okta SAML config. Priya will coordinate.
[06:49] Priya: Yep I'll ping our infra team.
[06:51] Maya: Cool. Quick recap before we close — Redwood provides 50k credits, security packet, benchmark script; Ravi runs bench with Jin's sample data; Priya shares network details; Ben lists compliance questions. We'll target results and a follow-up on 2026-07-29.
[07:06] Ben: Sounds good. One more thought — do you support streaming responses and function/tool calling? That's important for our chat agent.
[07:12] Lena: Yes, streaming and function calling are supported; we also have structured output tooling. We'll include doc links.
[07:19] Alex: Awesome, thanks everyone.
[07:22] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email.

AUTO-GENERATED ACTION NOTES:
- Maya to provision 50k free credits and quickstart docs.
- Ravi to draft bench script and schedule bench run with Jin.
- Lena to attach SOC2 and security whitepaper and detail KMS options.
- Priya to send VPC topology and Okta SAML config notes.

END OF TRANSCRIPT
